title: Who's the fat guy
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: Gully looks at the Daumier. 'Who's the fat guy.' A king. 'What'd he do.' Wood explains the July Monarchy for three panels. Gully draws the king as a walrus in the fourth. It's better.

panels.composition: The shack. The Daumier open on the counter — against rule four; nobody's drawing yet. GULLY looking. WOOD. BARNABY.

image.prompt: a heavy book of lithographs open on a bait shack counter, a stocky teenager looking at it, a young man and a dog nearby, black and white, no words

panels.composition: Wood, explaining. The balloon over the panel's edge.

balloons.text: Louis-Philippe. The July Monarchy. The bourgeois king. Daumier drew him as a pear and went to prison for six months—

image.prompt: a young man explaining something at length with his hands while a teenager listens patiently, black and white, no words

panels.composition: Gully, with a pen and a napkin, not listening.

image.prompt: close on a stocky teenager drawing on a napkin with a ballpoint pen, absorbed, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The napkin: the king as a walrus. In a crown. It's better. Wood's face, above it, knowing it's better.

image.prompt: close on a napkin with a ballpoint drawing of a walrus wearing a crown, a young man's face above it conceding, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: Gully's walrus king beats the explanation. Wood concedes with one word.
